newsitem.title: GERMANY: SAP spurs German share market to new records.
newsitem.headline: SAP spurs German share market to new records.

text.p: Strong results from software firm SAP AG and an overnight Wall Street rally spurred the German share market to new records on Friday.

The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade at a record close of 3,035.15 points, a rise of 17.83 points, after the IBIS DAX index set an alltime intraday high in pre-bourse screen trade of 3,050.88 points.

SAP took centre stage from the start after the blue-chip software group shocked the market by beating its own results forecasts for 1996 with profits up 40 percent at 567 million marks and sales up 38 percent at 3.72 billion.
Trading heavily through the day, SAP's preferred shares ended floor trade up nearly 11 percent at 246 marks.
SAP was once considered the darling of the stock market but had come under pressure in recent months after unexpectedly revising its profit outlook downward.
"It was a huge surprise. People were pouncing on SAP and it kept going through the day. This company must really have made an effort in the last quarter," one dealer said.
Meanwhile luxury carmaker Porsche AG clocked up an advance of 10.5 percent to 1,500 marks, after announcing a surge in first-half profits and strong demand for its new Boxster model.
The overall gains were underpinned by an overnight rally on Wall Street and a myriad of other solid market factors, including rising Bunds and a steady dollar.

Gains were, however partly limited by profit-taking on financials including DAX heavyweight Allianz AG Holding, the giant insurance group which had surged some six percent on the back of a Goldman Sachs upgrade Thursday.
Allianz, dropping around a quarter of its gains from Thursday, ended down 42 marks at 3,045 marks. Among other financials, Deutsche Bank closed down 95 pfennigs at 81.70 marks.
